newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes slightly down against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes slightly down against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed at 8.3012 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, slightly down from Monday's 8.3010, in quiet trading on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, dealers said.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.3010 and moved around 8.3010 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.3006 and a low of 8.3013 late in the session.
Trading was slower than Monday, with most done at 8.3010, traders said. Dealers said the yuan traded in a narrow range, with market sentiment cautious.

"Investors expect no more market-moving news this week after the announcement that the yuan would be convertible on the current account," one dealer said. "They stayed on the sidelines to see how the yuan would perform."

"Expectations of intervention by the central bank prevented the yuan from rising but strong buying at low levels made it hard for it to fall," a second dealer said. Dealers expect the yuan to continue narrow movements on Wednesday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2700 from 7.2930 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at an intra-day high of 1.0725 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
